p: Rivington owes much of its character to William Lever, the soap magnate who became Lord Leverhulme. He shaped Lever Park and left behind some wonderfully quirky features. Down by Rivington Reservoir you'll find a replica of the ruined Liverpool Castle, built as a deliberate folly, which makes a great photo stop and a fun place for kids to explore.

The old barns at Rivington, Great House Barn and Rivington Hall Barn, are historic buildings that have long been popular stops for walkers wanting a brew. Up on the hillside, the Pigeon Tower is one of the most recognisable features of the restored Terraced Gardens, and Winter Hill, with its tall TV mast, looms over the whole landscape.

For the Go Ape course, set aside a couple of hours and arrive early, because Rivington is hugely popular on sunny weekends and car parks fill up. If you can, choose a session in the morning, do the treetops while you're fresh, then head for the gardens and the Pike in the afternoon.

Rivington's paths can be steep and muddy in places, so wear something with real grip, both for the ropes and for the walking. Pack water, a snack for the top of the Pike and a jacket for the wind, which can be fierce up on the moors even on a mild day.
Chorley and Horwich are both close by, with plenty of places to grab a bite on the way home.
